headline: Khamenei peace signal sinks WTI below $100; gold rebounds to $4,060 as bonds mark time for the Fed
summary: Iran's supreme leader called for an end to the 'neither war nor peace' standoff, and December WTI fell $1.86 to $99.90 while RBOB dropped 2.5% to $3.1376, though Houthi missile claims on Riyadh and thin Gulf exports kept Brent near $114. Cheaper oil lifted gold about 1% to near $4,060 from an early $3,987 low and pulled silver off a near one-year low. Treasuries edged higher in yield on strong durable goods and confidence data despite a solid 5-year auction, while the OAT–Bund spread held near 156bp after a brief intraday widening.
drivers: Iran signals it wants the war ended

Khamenei met security chief Rezaei on Iran's conditions for ending the war, a day after Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani envoys visited Tehran. December WTI fell 1.8% to $99.90, its first close under $100 since Oct 22, and Brent lost $1.93 to $113.88.
Physical risk keeps a floor under crude

The Houthis claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's defence ministry, and tanker tracking shows Gulf crude exports down to about 65% of pre-war levels. UBS lifted its year-end Brent call to $110 from $100.
Strong US data offset a solid auction

Durable goods orders jumped 1.8% against 0.6% forecast and Conference Board confidence rose to 91.7 from 84.2, lifting the 2-year about 3bp to 4.74%. The $70bn 5-year sale cleared at 4.845%, far below September's 5.033%, with a 2.33 bid-to-cover, capping the 10-year near 5.00%.
Spot gold recovered from $3,987 to near $4,060, up about 1%, as lower crude eased inflation worries, even with the dollar at a two-week high and about 80% odds of a December Fed hike.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled down $1.86 (-1.8%) at $99.90, first close under $100 since Oct 22; Brent -$1.93 at $113.88.
oil.why: Crude fell for a second day after Iran's supreme leader met his top security official on the conditions for ending the war and said the 'neither war nor peace' state must end, following Monday's Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani talks in Tehran. WTI had traded up to $102.82 early. The drop stayed orderly because the Houthis claimed a missile hit on Riyadh and Gulf exports are only about 65% of pre-war levels; diesel fell 2.8% to $4.78.
oil.outlook: Bias lower but headline-driven: WTI $95–104, Brent $108–118. A concrete ceasefire framework would take WTI toward $95; a confirmed hit on Saudi export assets or Brent back above $117 would reopen the highs.
oil.watch: Iran talks, Houthi attacks, EIA stocks Oct 28, Dec Brent expiry Oct 30 and OPEC+ Nov 1.

gas.note: Nov RBOB fell 8.09¢ (-2.5%) to $3.1376, snapping a four-day winning streak; down about 8.7% this month.
gas.why: Gasoline tracked crude lower on the Iran peace signals, falling from an intraday high near $3.26 in its biggest one-day drop since Oct 2, as the thin November contract heads into Friday's expiry. Fundamentals are soft: pump prices have fallen five straight weeks to about $4.27 on AAA, and API data after the settle showed a 2.4 million barrel gasoline build against forecasts for a 0.7 million draw.
gas.outlook: Range $3.02–3.25; December trades several cents lower, so the roll drags the front-month quote down. An EIA build confirming API's would push toward $3.05; a rebound needs Brent back above $117.
gas.watch: EIA stocks Oct 28, Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30 and AAA's weekly pump average.

gold.note: Spot near $4,060, up about 1%, after an early dip to $3,987; Dec futures near $4,073.
gold.why: Gold slipped below $4,000 in early trade as the dollar hit a two-week high, then turned higher once crude broke toward $100 on Iran's peace signals, easing the inflation fears that have fed Fed hike bets. Zaner Metals said cheaper oil softens the hawkish case. The gain was contained because markets still price about an 80% chance of a December hike and the 10-year sits near 5%.
gold.outlook: Range $3,975–4,110 into the Fed. A statement that leaves December open plus a soft PCE would clear $4,110; a firm hike signal or hot PCE would retest $3,975, with $3,886 the key floor.
gold.watch: The Fed Oct 28, Q3 GDP and PCE Oct 29, and oil headlines.

silver.note: Spot near $54.4, up about 0.9%, recovering from a near one-year low around $53 earlier in the session.
silver.why: Silver hit its lowest in almost a year early, down about 2% as the firmer dollar and worries about industrial demand weighed, then rebounded with gold once oil slid. It still lagged on the day's lows, pushing the gold/silver ratio near 75, and platinum and palladium also touched multi-month lows, showing broad pressure on the metals complex from expected Fed tightening.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $52.80–56.00 range. A close below $53 targets $52 and then $50; it needs a close above $56 to signal a base.
silver.watch: The Fed Oct 28, big-tech earnings, PCE Oct 29 and China data.

us2y.note: Up about 3bp to near 4.74% on strong durable goods and confidence data.
us2y.why: The 2-year rose as September durable goods orders jumped 1.8%, three times the 0.6% forecast, though ex-transport orders rose only 0.5%, and Conference Board confidence beat with 91.7 against about 81 expected. That reinforced the 'hawkish hold' view: markets give about 91% odds the Fed stays at 3.75–4.00% on Wednesday but still price a December hike. Lower oil kept the move modest.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.65–4.82%. A Warsh press conference that points to December would lift it toward 4.82%; a softer tone or a cool PCE would pull it back to 4.65%.
us2y.watch: The Fed Oct 28, the 7-year auction, Q3 GDP and PCE Oct 29.

us5y.note: About 4.85%, up less than 1bp; $70bn auction cleared at 4.845%, a 0.3bp tail, with a 2.33 bid-to-cover.
us5y.why: The 5-year held steady as a strong auction offset the firm data. The $70bn sale cleared at 4.845%, a hair above the 4.842% when-issued but far below September's 5.033%, with a 2.33 bid-to-cover above the 2.31 average, a sign demand has recovered from early-October turmoil. Strong durable goods orders and confidence kept it from rallying.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.76–4.95%. A hawkish Fed would push it toward 4.95%; a soft PCE or relief on oil would test 4.76%.
us5y.watch: The Fed Oct 28, the 7-year auction and PCE Oct 29.

us10y.note: Near 5.00%, up about 1bp; stuck just under the 5% line ahead of the Fed.
us10y.why: The 10-year ended a touch higher as the beats on durable goods and consumer confidence outweighed the drag from oil falling below $100. Intraday lows came after the solid 5-year auction and a $6bn Treasury buyback of 20- and 30-year bonds, but buyers stayed cautious before Wednesday's Fed and Thursday's PCE. Pimco expects a hold with a clear tightening bias and one or two more hikes.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.88–5.10%. A hawkish Fed would hold it above 5%; a peace deal that sends oil lower or a soft PCE would test 4.88%.
us10y.watch: The Fed Oct 28, GDP and PCE Oct 29, the midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.

us30y.note: About 5.31%, up about 1bp; buybacks of long bonds limited the rise.
us30y.why: The long bond edged higher with the rest of the curve on firm data, but the Treasury's $6bn buyback of 20- and 30-year debt and cheaper oil, which trims inflation compensation, kept the move small. Term-premium concerns around the midterms and next week's refunding remain the main upside risk.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.20–5.42%. Smaller long-bond sizes at the refunding would help it rally; a hawkish Fed plus unchanged sizes would push it toward 5.40%.
us30y.watch: The Fed Oct 28, the midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.

de2y.note: About 3.06%, up under 1bp after dipping 3bp intraday; ECB hold priced for Thursday.
de2y.why: The Schatz dipped early as the ECB's bank lending survey showed rate hikes biting, with a net 27% of banks reporting weaker mortgage demand against 12% expected, then recovered as US data firmed. Markets expect the ECB to hold its 2.50% deposit rate on Thursday but price roughly a 75% chance of a December hike with inflation at 3.8%.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.98–3.15%. A Lagarde signal for December would lift it toward 3.15%; emphasis on tighter credit or French stress would test 2.98%.
de2y.watch: The ECB Oct 29 and flash October inflation at the end of the week.

de5y.note: About 3.17%, up about 0.5bp, little changed in a pre-ECB session.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund was steady as softer oil and the weak bank lending survey, which pointed to rate hikes cooling credit, balanced firmer US yields. Some haven buying returned briefly when French yields jumped in the morning, but it faded as the OAT recovered.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.08–3.25%. A hawkish ECB would push it to the top; renewed French stress would bring back the haven bid.
de5y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, euro-area inflation and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: About 3.35%, roughly flat; spread to OATs near 156bp after widening to about 161bp intraday.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund ended flat after falling about 1.5bp in the morning, when investors sold French debt again after Monday's Moody's relief rally and bought German paper. That haven bid faded as the OAT recovered and US yields rose on strong data, while oil's slide below $100 eased inflation concerns.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.28–3.45%. A hawkish ECB or firm data tilt it higher; a dovish ECB or a fresh French selloff would cap it.
de10y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, euro inflation and French budget votes.

de30y.note: About 3.69%, little changed with the US long end.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund was steady as cheaper oil offset a slight rise in US long yields. It tracks global term premium and German fiscal expansion more than ECB pricing, so a quiet session for long Treasuries kept it in range.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.80%. It follows US long bonds and German supply more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US long yields, the Nov 4 refunding and German long-dated sales.

fr2y.note: About 3.73%, up about 2bp as part of Monday's Moody's rally faded.
fr2y.why: Short French debt gave back some of its gains as the relief from Moody's hold wore off and investors refocused on the 2027 budget fight. The ECB's survey showed credit tightening was sharpest in France among large members, a reminder of the growth cost of higher yields. The front end stays anchored by ECB pricing, which limited the move.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.65–3.82%. It stays anchored by the ECB unless the budget fails or a censure motion threatens the government.
fr2y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, French flash inflation and the budget debate.

fr5y.note: About 4.34%, up about 2bp after Monday's sharp rally.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT edged higher as some investors took profits on the post-Moody's rally. Deficit forecasts of 5.4% of GDP this year, a minority government and the lower house's rejection of the social security bill keep buyers selective, while the IMF's cut to its 2026 French growth forecast to 0.4% adds to fiscal doubts.
fr5y.outlook: Range 4.22–4.45%. A budget setback in parliament or new unrest would send it back toward 4.45%.
fr5y.watch: The budget debate, the ECB Oct 29 and French inflation data.

fr10y.note: About 4.92%, up about 1bp after rising 5bp intraday; spread to Bunds near 156bp.
fr10y.why: The 10-year OAT jumped about 5bp to near 4.96% in the morning as the Moody's relief faded and the spread to Bunds widened back to about 161bp. It retraced most of that by the close as oil fell below $100 and European stocks rallied, leaving the spread near 156bp. Lagarde's comments on French spreads on Thursday are the next test.
fr10y.outlook: Spread range 145–170bp with a bias to hold 150–160bp. A failed budget vote or fresh unrest would put 167bp back in play; a reassuring ECB message would help it narrow toward 150bp.
fr10y.watch: The ECB Oct 29, budget votes in parliament, French inflation and S&P's review Nov 27.

fr30y.note: About 5.41%, little changed, holding just below last week's highs.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT was steady as profit-taking on Monday's rally was offset by cheaper oil and firmer risk appetite. Investors still demand a large premium for long French debt through the budget fight and the 2027 presidential race, with debt near 120% of GDP keeping the long end the most exposed point on the curve.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.30–5.55%. A credible budget deal would extend the rally; a close above 5.55% would signal the relief has run out.
fr30y.watch: The budget debate, long-dated OAT auctions and the ECB Oct 29.

watch: Next: the Fed decision and EIA stocks Oct 28, the ECB, US Q3 GDP, PCE and the 7-year auction Oct 29, Nov RBOB and Dec Brent expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ on Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.
